_source.description: Major global manganese mining and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-manganese.pdf); USGS Mineral Resources Data System (https://mrdata.usgs.gov/mrds/); S&P Global Market Intelligence mine profiles; South32 (ASX: S32) Annual Report 2023; Eramet (EPA: ERA) Annual Report 2023; Assmang (ARM/Assore JV) Annual Report 2023; United Manganese of Kalahari (UMK) company disclosures; Ghana Manganese Company annual reports; Vale (NYSE: VALE) Annual Report 2023; MOIL Ltd (BSE: 533286) Annual Report 2023; Consolidated Minerals annual reports; OM Holdings (SGX: OMH) annual reports; Privat Group (Ukraine) public disclosures; Autlan (BMV: AUTLAN) Annual Report 2023; Mesa Minerals/OM Manganese annual reports
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Major manganese ore operations globally — operating mines, advanced development projects, and significant deposits. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, technical reports, and satellite verification. Production/capacity figures from 2023 where available. Capacity figures in manganese ore tonnes per annum unless otherwise noted.

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — 21 million tonnes manganese ore
_coverage.known_gaps: Smaller Chinese operations in Guizhou, Hunan, and Yunnan provinces (~15% of global supply from numerous small mines); artisanal mining in Zambia and Cote d'Ivoire; smaller Indian operations outside MOIL

sites.name: Hotazel (Mamatwan + Wessels Complex)
sites.notes: World's largest manganese operation; Mamatwan is open-pit (lower grade), Wessels is underground (high grade); Kalahari Manganese Field contains ~70% of global reserves

sites.name: N'Chwaning Mine
sites.ownership: African Rainbow Minerals (50%), Assore (50%) via Assmang
sites.notes: Underground mine in northern Kalahari Manganese Field; high-grade metallurgical ore; N'Chwaning II and III shafts

sites.name: Gloria Mine
sites.notes: One of the largest open-pit manganese mines in the Kalahari Basin; exports via Saldanha Bay

sites.name: Tshipi Borwa Mine
sites.notes: Large open-pit mine; one of the lowest-cost manganese producers globally; commissioned 2012

sites.name: Nchwaning/Gloria (Black Rock)
sites.ownership: African Rainbow Minerals (50%), Assore (50%) via Assmang
sites.notes: Black Rock mining complex encompasses multiple shafts in the Kalahari Manganese Field; includes sinter and alloy plants

sites.name: Kalagadi Mine
sites.notes: Open-pit mine in the central Kalahari Manganese Field; underground extension development

sites.name: Moanda Mine
sites.notes: One of the world's largest and highest-grade manganese deposits; open-pit; ore transported via Trans-Gabon Railway to Owendo port; Comilog operates since 1962

sites.name: GEMCO (Groote Eylandt)
sites.notes: Groote Eylandt Mining Company; island mine in Gulf of Carpentaria, NT; one of the world's highest-grade deposits; operating since 1966

sites.name: Bootu Creek
sites.notes: Open-pit mine ~110km north of Tennant Creek, NT; medium-grade ore; variable production levels

sites.name: Woodie Woodie
sites.notes: Open-pit mine in the East Pilbara, WA; high-grade manganese oxide ore; operating since 2000

sites.name: Nsuta Mine
sites.notes: Oldest manganese mine in sub-Saharan Africa; operating since 1916; Western Region of Ghana; exports via Takoradi port

sites.name: Azul (Carajas)
sites.notes: Open-pit mine in the Carajas mineral province, Para state; integrated with Vale's Carajas iron ore logistics

sites.name: Urucum
sites.notes: Near Corumba, Mato Grosso do Sul; manganese and iron ore deposit in Urucum Massif; river transport via Paraguay-Parana waterway

sites.name: Morro da Mina
sites.notes: Near Conselheiro Lafaiete, Minas Gerais; one of the oldest Mn mines in Brazil; carbonate ore used for chemical/battery grade

sites.name: Zunyi (Songtao District)
sites.notes: Songtao County, Guizhou Province; largest manganese mining district in China; numerous underground mines; lower grade than African ores

sites.name: Daxin Mine
sites.notes: Daxin County, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; integrated mining and electrolytic manganese production

sites.name: Tiandeng Mine
sites.notes: Tiandeng County, Guangxi; part of the Guangxi manganese mining belt; underground operations

sites.name: Jingxi (Baise) Mines
sites.notes: Jingxi City area, Guangxi; multiple underground mines; part of China's southern manganese district

sites.name: Xiangtan EMM Complex
sites.notes: Xiangtan, Hunan Province; major EMM processing center; processes imported and domestic ore; China produces ~95% of global EMM

sites.name: Balaghat Mine
sites.ownership: Government of India (majority, via MOIL Ltd, BSE: 533286)
sites.notes: MOIL's largest underground mine; Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh; high-grade manganese ore

sites.name: Dongri Buzurg Mine
sites.ownership: Government of India (majority, via MOIL Ltd)
sites.notes: Underground mine in Bhandara district, Maharashtra; second-largest MOIL operation

sites.name: Gumgaon Mine
sites.ownership: Government of India (majority, via MOIL Ltd)
sites.notes: Open-pit mine near Nagpur, Maharashtra; MOIL's largest open-pit operation

sites.name: Munsar Mine
sites.ownership: Government of India (majority, via MOIL Ltd)
sites.notes: Open-pit mine in Nagpur district, Maharashtra

sites.name: Tirodi Mine
sites.ownership: Government of India (majority, via MOIL Ltd)
sites.notes: Underground mine in Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh

sites.name: Nikopol Basin
sites.ownership: Privat Group (controlled by Ihor Kolomoisky affiliates)
sites.notes: World's second-largest manganese reserve base after Kalahari; Nikopol-Marganets basin; production disrupted by Russia-Ukraine conflict since 2022; historically ~10% of global supply

sites.name: Velykyi Tokmak
sites.notes: Zaporizhzhia Oblast; eastern extension of Nikopol manganese basin; severely disrupted by conflict; located near front lines since 2022

sites.name: Molango Mine
sites.notes: Hidalgo state; largest manganese deposit in North America; Autlan operates integrated mine-to-alloy facilities

sites.name: Tambao Mine
sites.notes: High-grade deposit in Sahel Region; requires 330km rail link to Kaya; development stalled by infrastructure requirements and political instability

sites.name: Ansongo Project
sites.notes: Near Ansongo, Gao Region; high-grade manganese deposit in the Tilemsi Valley; development limited by security situation in northern Mali

sites.name: Kisenge Mine
sites.notes: Katanga Province; historically significant deposit; operations suspended since 1990s; rehabilitation planned

sites.name: Mansa Mine (Manganese)
sites.notes: Luapula Province; relatively new mining operation in Zambia's manganese belt

sites.name: Woodie Woodie North (Ant Hill)
sites.notes: Satellite deposit north of main Woodie Woodie operation; East Pilbara, WA

sites.name: Butcherbird Project
sites.notes: Pilbara region, WA; low-grade but large tonnage deposit; beneficiation to produce high-purity manganese sulphate for battery market

sites.name: Selabora (Selangor) Mine
sites.notes: Malaysia is a significant manganese ore producer (~200kt/yr); numerous small operations in Perak, Kelantan, and Terengganu; fragmented industry

sites.name: Ust-Kamenogorsk (EMM Plant)
sites.notes: East Kazakhstan; ERG operates integrated manganese mining and alloy production from Kazakh deposits; significant ferroalloy exporter

sites.name: Atasurda Mine (Central Kazakhstan)
sites.notes: Karaganda region; part of Kazakhstan's central manganese belt; ore supplies domestic ferroalloy industry

sites.name: Mabounié Project
sites.notes: Polymetallic deposit ~30km from Moanda; feasibility studies ongoing; potential Mn-Nb-REE co-production

sites.name: Grassy Mountain Project
sites.notes: Juab County, Utah; one of few US manganese projects; the US currently imports 100% of its manganese; development-stage with intermittent activity
